reuse.why: Builds on the existing getScheduledAmount and getApproxNumberThreshold, and the API field reuses the same helper rather than re-deriving the rule.

duplication.why: Removes the five copies of the midpoint expression (schedules/app.ts x2, forecast-schedules.ts, schedule-template.ts, computeSchedulePreviewTransactions) in favour of one getPlannedAmount.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts beside getScheduledAmount; expectedAmount is attached in the api.ts handler rather than in scheduleModel.toExternal, a small placement choice.

scope.why: Focused on the amount rule, its consumers and the API field; one comment in computeSchedulePreviewTransactions is left stale ('end furthest from zero').

maintainability.why: Small named functions (getRangeAmount, getApproxAmount, getPlannedAmount) with getScheduledAmount as a thin sign wrapper make the rule a one-place change, as step 4 shows.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All server and client consumers route through getPlannedAmount/getScheduledAmount.

disguised_duplication.where: None; copies were removed, not reshaped.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gains an op parameter and getPlannedAmount an isapprox branch for the approximate-amount step; every call site (including forecast, schedule-template, postTransactionForSchedule, preview, API list and the desktop components) uses it.
